title: service-scoped-trace-enforcement-and-retention-slas
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Introduce service-scoped enforcement for traces and metrics ingestion: classify incoming spans/logs, apply service-specific retention SLAs, and enable query-safe outputs while preserving debuggability. This ticket implements an enforcement layer at the telemetry ingress that tags, masks, or rejects sensitive signals per service policy and records auditable access for any later reveal requests.
acceptance_criteria: Ingestion layer applies service-level data classification and enforces configured retention windows on spans and log events
Sensitive fields in span attributes and logs are masked or tokenized according to service policy with reversible tokens stored in an encrypted reveal store
RBAC-controlled Just-In-Time (JIT) reveal flow exists: operators can request temporary access; requests are logged to an immutable audit stream
Tracing dashboards reflect both full and sanitized views depending on viewer permissions, without exposing raw PII to viewers lacking approval
Latency overhead at ingestion remains <5ms p95 for standard trace envelopes after enforcement layer is enabled
End-to-end integration tests covering classification rules, retention triggers, and reveal flow are present in CI
implementation_notes: Add a lightweight classification hook in the telemetry ingress (Go) that inspects span tags and log records against a per-service ruleset pulled from the policy service
Ruleset format: allow simple regex plus named-presence / numeric-range checks to keep eval cheap at ingest
Masking strategy: deterministic keyed HMAC truncated token for indexable fields; reversible envelope with KMS-protected key for full reveal when allowed
Retention enforcement: write-to-tier metadata on each event (hot/short, warm/30d, cold/365d) and run a TTL sweeper that consults service SLA; do not rely on downstream storage alone
RBAC: integrate with existing SSO groups; create 'telemetry-reveal' permission scoped per service and per environment
Audit: append reveal requests and decisions to immutable audit stream (Kafka topic with retention) and surface summary in Console
Performance: prototype eBPF-based sampling for high-throughput services as a follow-up if p95 ingestion exceeds 5ms
Fallback behavior: when policy service is unreachable, enforce conservative default (mask and short retention) and add a routed metric/alert
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — small Go-based ingress hook prototype classifies spans and applies HMAC tokenization. p95 added ~2.1ms on local harness
2026-03-05: Design review with Privacy & Security — agreed on reversible reveal only via KMS-wrapped envelope and strict RBAC gating
2026-03-08: End-to-end test harness created; demoed masking + reveal flow using test policy for 'payments-service'
2026-03-11: Implementation PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/PR-2384); initial CI failing on audit-stream schema validation — investigating
2026-03-13: Resolved schema mismatch; deployment to staging scheduled 2026-03-16 behind feature flag 'service-scope-enforce'
review_feedback: S. Morales (Security): Ensure key rotation path for reversible envelopes; do not allow long-lived plaintext fallback
A. Chen (Platform): Recommend adding per-service sampling overrides to avoid cost spikes for high-cardinality masking tokens
D. Martínez (Observability): Dashboard UX should expose a clear indicator when data is masked and provide a safe 'request reveal' CTA linking to the audit page
PM note (E. Park): Prioritize payments & healthcare services for initial rollout due to regulatory risk
notes: Plan phased rollout: start with opt-in for low-traffic services, then opt-out window for high-risk services
Follow-up tickets: sampling policy UI in Console, schema for reveal audit export (CSV/JSON), and eBPF sampling spike
Consider a 'synthetic-safe' mode for CI traces where full payloads are retained but marked as non-production
